name: Nambla
confidence_why: The only phonological description of Nambla, Arman 2020, says stress, tone and length are all non-contrastive but never states where stress falls, its one hint (length always on the first syllable, long allophones in stressed open syllables whose examples are all word-initial) pointing loosely to the first syllable, and the only other work read, Lee and Lebold 2017, says nothing about Nambla stress.
catalog_citation: Arman [Mappiasse]. 2020. Phonology of Nambla language in Keerom Papua / Fonologi bahasa Nambla di Keerom Papua. Kibas Cenderawasih 17(1): 1-16. doi:10.26499/kc.v17i1.241 (journal PDF via web.archive.org snapshot 20220728011714)
catalog_locator: sec. 4 Conclusion, p.15 (suprasegmentals); sec. 3.6.2 Vowel Variation, pp.10-11 (long allophones in stressed open syllables)
catalog_quote: Based on the data, although there are suprasegmental elements in Nambla language such as stress, tone, and duration, but there are no distinctive suprasegmental elements or distinguishing meaning. Therefore, it can be concluded that there are no suprasegmental phonemes in Nambla language. Regarding duration, the suprasegmental elements, always located in the first syllable. ... [sec. 3.6.2] Phoneme /e/ has variations or allophones [E:], and [e]. The variations occur in accordance with their respective environments, i.e.: [E:], occurs in open syllables that under pressure; [e], occurs in other places. Example: /E:li/ /E:li/ 'naked' /peiye/ /pe.i.ye/ 'moon' ... Phoneme /O/ has variations or allophones [O:] and [O]. ... [O:], occurs in open syllables that under pressure; [O], occurs in other places. Example: /fO:lame/ /fO:.la.me/ 'old' /lumbO/ /lum.bO/ 'heart' ... Phoneme /a/ has variation…

audit.reasoning: Quote check passes: both deciding passages are verbatim in the PDF we hold at the stated pages (p.15 conclusion; pp.10-11 vowel variation). The deciding source is a 2020 segmental phonology article, the sole phonological description of this ~30-speaker language in Glottolog and on the web; nothing better exists, and it is. Its prosodic content is a single conclusion sentence (stress non-contrastive; 'duration.. always located in the first syllable') plus long-vowel allophones 'in open syllables under pressure' whose examples are all word-initial, so the catalog's 'undetermined' with an implied-initial note is the faithful reading; no source suggests a different coding. The record cannot be 'well-sourced' because the source itself gives no stress rule, but it is not at risk. The one open item downloaded now (SIL ESR 2016-008 Emem survey) is silent on Namla prosody. works still to obtain are low
